title: Article 310 — Tenure of office of persons serving the Union or a State

content.overview: Article 310 provides that, except as expressly provided by the Constitution, every person who is a member of a defence service or of a civil service of the Union or of an all-India service or holds any post connected with defence or any civil post under the Union holds office during the pleasure of the President, and every person who is a member of a civil service of a State or holds any civil post under a State holds office during the pleasure of the Governor of the State. Notwithstanding that a person holds office during pleasure, any contract under which a person not being a member of a defence service or of an all-India service or of a civil service of the Union or a State is appointed under this Constitution may provide for compensation if the post is abolished or the person is required to vacate before expiration of an agreed period.
content.glance: Doctrine of pleasure: Union civil/defence posts — pleasure of President; State civil posts — pleasure of Governor. Contractual compensation possible for certain non-service appointments.
content.study:
Article 310 embodies the doctrine of pleasure:
- Union (defence services, civil services of the Union, all-India services, defence-connected posts, civil posts under the Union): during the pleasure of the President.
- State (civil services of a State, civil posts under a State): during the pleasure of the Governor.
- Exception for contractual terms on compensation where a person not belonging to the listed services is appointed under a contract and the post is abolished or early vacation is required.

Pleasure is subject to constitutional limitations, especially Article 311 safeguards for civil servants.

Examination: pleasure of President vs Governor; all-India services under President; Art 311 as a restriction on pleasure; contractual compensation limb.

sections.heading: Key rules
sections.body:
1. Union services/posts (including all-India services): office during pleasure of the President.
2. State civil services/posts: office during pleasure of the Governor.
3. Limited contractual compensation for certain non-service contract appointments.
4. Pleasure subject to Art 311 and other constitutional constraints.

questionsAndAnswers.question: Explain the doctrine of pleasure under Article 310.
questionsAndAnswers.answer: Under Article 310, except as expressly provided by the Constitution, members of defence services, civil services of the Union, all-India services, and holders of defence-connected or civil posts under the Union hold office during the pleasure of the President, and members of civil services of a State and holders of civil posts under a State hold office during the pleasure of the Governor. This pleasure is subject to constitutional safeguards, notably Article 311. A limited contractual provision for compensation may apply where a person not belonging to those services is appointed under contract and the post is abolished or early vacation is required.

examTips: Pleasure of President (Union/AIS) / Governor (State); limited by Art 311.

keyTakeaways: Art 310: doctrine of pleasure — President/Governor; subject to Art 311.
